text_blocks.snippet: The ICD-10-CM code I25.2 is used to denote Old myocardial infarction. This code is appropriate when the myocardial infarction (heart attack) occurred more than 28 days ago. If the MI was within the past 28 days, other MI codes would be applicable.

list.title: Definition:

list.title: Timeframe:

list.title: Documentation:

text_blocks.snippet: The primary ICD-10-CM code for a heart attack (myocardial infarction) is I21. Within this category, further codes specify the type and location of the infarction. For example, I21.3 is for ST elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) of unspecified site, while I21.4 is for non-ST elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI). Subsequent myocardial infarctions within 4 weeks of a previous one are coded under I22.

list.snippet: I21: This is the main category for acute myocardial infarction.
I21.3: STEMI (ST elevation) myocardial infarction of unspecified site.
I22: Subsequent myocardial infarction (within 4 weeks of a previous one).

text_blocks.snippet: When coding, it's crucial to be as specific as possible, indicating whether it's STEMI or NSTEMI and the location of the infarction, if documented. Additionally, if it's a subsequent infarction, the I22 codes should be used in conjunction with the initial I21 code.
